mainTopic: Completeness of the משנה's list, where עננו is said, which fasts pregnant and nursing women keep, and what הַתְרָעָה means
overview: The גמרא finishes its discussion of whether the משנה's list of differences for the last seven fasts is complete. In the end it rules that items taught in another chapter, the תיבה and the twenty-four blessings, do not count as omissions. It then rules that an individual says עננו in שומע תפילה. Next, three ברייתות seem to disagree about whether pregnant and nursing women fast. רב אשי resolves them all: these women fast only on the middle set of fasts. The גמרא then asks what the משנה's 'sounding the alarm' (הַתְרָעָה) means: blowing שופרות, or the prayer עננו. It concludes that everyone counts שופרות as הַתְרָעָה, and the argument is only about whether עננו also counts. A ברייתא challenges the עננו view. The גמרא answers that this is a dispute between תנאים, proven from a משנה that allows sounding the alarm on שבת, which must mean עננו because שופר is not blown on שבת. The amud ends by opening a story about a time of trouble in the days of רבי יהודה נשיאה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה also left out the ark
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the claim that the משנה's list is incomplete: it never mentions the תיבה being taken out.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה left out the ark!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings evidence that the תנא did not list everything, because the משנה never mentions taking the תיבה out to the street.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the last seven fasts the תיבה (ark) was brought out into the town square. That is a real difference from the earlier fasts, yet the משנה's list does not include it. So the list seems to be incomplete (תנא ושייר).

keyTerms.meaning: The ark holding the Torah scrolls, brought out to the street on severe fasts
The תנא taught some items and left others out

phrases.english: But he omitted the ark!
phrases.notes: Supports the claim that the list is not complete

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of whether the משנה's list is complete
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's list of differences is not complete (תנא ושייר)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה does not mention the תיבה being taken out

steps.title: Public practices are not listed here
steps.stepSummary: Leaving out the תיבה is not a real omission, because the משנה only lists private practices, not public ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is because of the ark, that is not an omission. The תנא teaches private matters and does not teach public matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof: the תיבה was never meant to be on this list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's list covers things done in private, such as sounding the alarm and saying the twenty-four blessings, which רש״י explains are done inside the בית הכנסת. Bringing the תיבה out is a public, outdoor event, so it falls into a different category. Its absence therefore does not prove that the list is incomplete.

phrases.english: If it is because of the ark —
that is not an omission.
Private matters, he teaches;
public matters, he does not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם תֵּיבָה לָאו שִׁיּוּרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the תיבה
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the תיבה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The תיבה belongs to public practices, which the משנה never meant to list

steps.title: רב אשי: the משנה's wording supports this
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the משנה's wording, 'what is more about these… only… but everything else is the same,' shows that the list is meant to be complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The משנה is also precise, since it teaches: 'How are these more severe than the first ones? Only that on these they sound the alarm and lock the stores. But in all their other matters, both are the same.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings support from the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the only differences are sounding the alarm and locking stores, and that 'everything else is the same.' That wording sounds like a complete list. So nothing that would make the later fasts stricter, such as the twenty-four blessings, was left out.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה's wording also proves this
They sound the alarm (blow shofars / cry out)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The mishna is also precise, as it teaches:
How are these more stringent than the first ones?
Only that on these they sound the alarm
and lock the stores.
But in all their other matters —
both this and that are the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds support from the wording of the משנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording 'מה אלו… אלא… אבל בכל דבריהן זה וזה שוין'

steps.title: רב אשי blocks the claim that this list is incomplete
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי heads off the reply that this list also leaves things out: the phrase 'מה אלו' shows it is exact.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that here too he taught and omitted, but it says 'How are these…'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes his proof by blocking an expected objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might answer that this list is also partial. רב אשי says the phrase 'מה אלו', 'in what way are these different', signals an exact and complete answer.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי תְּנָא וְשַׁיַּיר,
phrases.english: And if you say here too he taught and omitted,
but it teaches 'How are these.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי תְּנָא וְשַׁיַּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב אשי's proof by heading off a reply
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The possible claim that this list is also incomplete
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase 'מה אלו' signals a complete list

steps.title: Is 'how are these' really exact? The ark is missing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי: 'מה אלו' cannot be exact, because the תיבה is not mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do you think 'How are these' is exact? But it left out the ark!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אשי's reading of the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer, that public matters are not listed, was not enough here. 'מה אלו' claims to list every difference, and the תיבה is still a difference. So the phrase cannot be read as fully exact.

keyTerms.meaning: And do you really think so?

phrases.english: And do you think 'How are these' is exact?
But he omitted the ark!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's proof
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that 'מה אלו' means the list is complete
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A complete list could not leave out the תיבה, yet it does

steps.title: The ark is taught in another chapter
steps.stepSummary: The תיבה is not a real omission, because the תנא teaches it in the next chapter.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is because of the ark, that is not an omission, because he counts it in the other chapter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a new reason the תיבה is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is no longer the public-versus-private distinction. Now the reason is that the next chapter (15a) discusses the תיבה. The תנא does not need to repeat here what he teaches fully there.

phrases.english: If it is because of the ark —
that is not an omission,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא חָשֵׁיב לַהּ בְּאִידַּךְ פִּרְקָא.
phrases.english: because he lists it in the other chapter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם תֵּיבָה לָאו שִׁיּוּרָא הוּא מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא חָשֵׁיב לַהּ בְּאִידַּךְ פִּרְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against 'מה אלו'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaving out the תיבה proves the list is incomplete
steps.terutzMaskana: Items taught in another chapter are not counted as omissions

steps.title: The 24 blessings are also not an omission
steps.stepSummary: Using the same logic, the twenty-four blessings are also not an omission, since they are taught in the other chapter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this: the twenty-four blessings are also not an omission, since he teaches them in the other chapter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies its new answer to the earlier question about the twenty-four blessings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If anything taught elsewhere does not count as an omission, then the twenty-four blessings, also taught on 15a, are not missing either. So רב אשי's precise reading no longer settles the question. The proof becomes neutral.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have arrived at this
The twenty-four blessings of the fast-day תפילה

steps.whatToRemember: An item the תנא teaches in a different chapter is not called an 'omission.' This answer explains both the תיבה and the twenty-four blessings, so the wording of the משנה proves nothing either way.

phrases.english: Now that you have arrived at this:

phrases.aramaic: עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה נָמֵי לָאו שִׁיּוּרָא הוּא,
phrases.english: the twenty-four is also not an omission,
since he teaches it in the other chapter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the answer about the תיבה to the twenty-four blessings
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's list cannot settle the question, because items taught elsewhere are not considered omissions

steps.title: So what is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: Since no proof was conclusive, the גמרא asks what the ruling is about where עננו is inserted.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the conclusion about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the final ruling by asking what we actually do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the attempted proofs ended without a decision. So the גמרא turns to the אמוראים for a practical answer about where an individual says עננו.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the conclusion about it?

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the failed proofs to asking for a ruling
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where an individual inserts עננו in the עמידה

steps.title: First view: between 'Redeemer' and 'Healer'
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר סיסרטאי, and likewise רב חייא בר אשי in the name of רב, say עננו goes between the blessings גואל ישראל and רופא חולי עמו ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר סיסרטאי said, and so said רב חייא בר אשי in the name of רב: between 'Redeemer' and 'Healer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer: עננו is a separate blessing between the seventh and eighth blessings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view, עננו stands as its own section after גואל ישראל, as the חזן does on a fast day.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Sisretai said,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: and so said Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi in the name of Rav:
between 'Redeemer' and 'Healer.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question

steps.title: Second view: in 'Who listens to prayer'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי, quoting רבי ינאי son of רבי ישמעאל, says עננו is included in the blessing שומע תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אשי said in the name of רבי ינאי son of רבי ישמעאל: in 'Who listens to prayer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, competing answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view the individual does not add a new section. Instead, he includes עננו inside the general request blessing שומע תפילה.

phrases.english: And Rav Ashi said in the name of
Rabbi Yannai, son of Rabbi Yishmael:
in 'Who listens to prayer.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first answer

steps.title: The law: in 'Who listens to prayer'
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that an individual says עננו in שומע תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: in 'Who listens to prayer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the practical law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of the two views, the הלכה follows רבי ינאי. The individual includes עננו within שומע תפילה.
steps.whatToRemember: An individual fasting says עננו inside the blessing שומע תפילה, not as a separate blessing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice today: an individual inserts עננו in שומע תפילה on a fast day.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: in 'Who listens to prayer.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two views
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עננו is said in שומע תפילה

steps.title: Three teachings that seem to clash about pregnant and nursing women
steps.stepSummary: Three ברייתות give three different rulings about whether pregnant and nursing women fast on the first fasts, the last fasts, or neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: pregnant and nursing women fast on the first fasts but not on the last fasts. Another ברייתא teaches: they fast on the last fasts but not on the first fasts. And yet another ברייתא teaches: they do not fast at all, neither on the first nor on the last.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lines up three ברייתות that seem to say opposite things about pregnant and nursing women on the public fasts. It is setting up a puzzle that the next step will solve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Remember there are three sets of fasts for rain: a first set of three, a middle set of three, and a last set of seven. The first ברייתא says they fast on the 'first' fasts, the second says they fast on the 'last' fasts, and the third says they fast on neither. On the surface all three cannot be true.

keyTerms.meaning: The first fasts / the last fasts

steps.confusionAlert: Do not picture only two sets of fasts. There are three: first, middle, and last. Keeping the middle set in mind is the key to the next step.

phrases.english: One baraita teaches:
Pregnant and nursing women fast on the first fasts,
but they do not fast on the last fasts.
And another baraita teaches: they fast on the last fasts,
but they do not fast on the first fasts.
And yet another baraita teaches: they do not fast,
neither on the first nor on the last.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the conclusion about עננו in שומע תפילה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the three ברייתות about pregnant and nursing women.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Three sources give three opposite rulings on the same case, so they appear to contradict each other.

steps.title: רב אשי: hold on to the middle fasts and everything fits
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that pregnant and nursing women fast only on the middle set, and that this reading resolves all three ברייתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Take the middle fasts in your hand, because with that all of the ברייתות are resolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי solves the contradiction. He says the ruling is that these women fast only on the middle three fasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא's 'first fasts' means the middle set, because it comes first compared to the last seven. The second ברייתא's 'last fasts' also means the middle set, because it comes last compared to the opening three. The third ברייתא uses 'first' and 'last' literally, meaning the opening three and the final seven, and on those they do not fast.

keyTerms.meaning: Take it in your hand, i.e., hold on to this as the rule
The middle ones (the middle set of fasts)

steps.whatToRemember: Pregnant and nursing women fast only on the middle three fasts. 'First' and 'last' are relative terms, so all three ברייתות agree.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Take the middle fasts in your hand,
for with this all of them are resolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relative reading of terms: 'first' and 'last' are read relative to different sets of fasts.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each ברייתא uses 'first' and 'last' in the same absolute sense, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two ברייתות are talking about the middle set from different angles. The third uses the terms literally. All three agree that the women fast only on the middle fasts.

steps.title: The משנה: the last seven fasts add an alarm and closed shops
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה saying the last seven fasts differ from the earlier ones because they sound an alarm and lock the shops.
steps.simpleTranslation: How are these last fasts more severe than the first ones? Only in that on these they sound the alarm and lock the shops.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes the line about the last seven fasts. It is setting up a question about what 'sounding the alarm' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists two new stringencies for the last seven fasts: מתריעין (sounding an alarm) and closing the stores. The word מתריעין is unclear, and the next step asks what it means.

keyTerms.meaning: They sound an alarm / cry out

phrases.english: How are these more stringent than the first ones?
Only that on these they sound the alarm
and they lock the shops.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה, separate from the women's fasting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the last seven fasts, beyond the earlier stringencies, they sound an alarm and close the shops.

steps.title: What is the alarm made with?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what instrument or method the משנה means by 'sounding the alarm.'
steps.simpleTranslation: With what do they sound the alarm?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question: what exactly is this 'alarm'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word התרעה can mean blowing a horn or crying out in prayer. The גמרא wants to know which one the משנה means.

phrases.english: With what do they sound the alarm?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of מתריעין from the משנה quoted in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of התרעה: a שופר blast or a spoken prayer.

steps.title: רב יהודה: with שופרות
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that the alarm is sounded with שופרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: With שופרות.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: the alarm means blowing שופרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב יהודה, the alarm is a physical sound made with a horn, not a prayer.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: With shofarot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 15.

steps.title: In the name of רב: with עננו
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, the son of רב שמואל בר שילת, says in the name of רב that the alarm is the prayer עננו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה, son of רב שמואל בר שילת, said in the name of רב: With עננו.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer: the 'alarm' is crying out in the prayer עננו ('Answer us').
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this view, התרעה is a cry of prayer, not a horn blast. This is the same עננו discussed earlier on the daf.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Answer us,' a prayer said on fast days

steps.confusionAlert: There are two people named רב יהודה here. The second is רב יהודה the son of רב שמואל בר שילת, and he is quoting רב.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת
phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat,
said in the name of Rav:
With Aneinu.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A competing answer to the same question answered in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: התרעה means saying the prayer עננו.

steps.title: First assumption: the two opinions exclude each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states its initial assumption that whoever says עננו rejects שופרות, and whoever says שופרות rejects עננו.
steps.simpleTranslation: It entered our mind that the one who said 'with עננו' did not say 'with שופרות,' and the one who said 'with שופרות' did not say 'with עננו.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out how it first understood the argument: each side completely rejects the other's method. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase קא סלקא דעתן signals a first impression that may later be revised. Here it means that, as things stand, the view of רב leaves no room for שופרות at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It entered our mind (our first assumption was)

phrases.english: It entered our mind:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר בַּ״עֲנֵנוּ״ — לָא אָמַר בְּשׁוֹפָרוֹת,
phrases.english: the one who said 'with Aneinu' did not say 'with shofarot,'

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר בְּשׁוֹפָרוֹת — לָא אָמַר בַּ״עֲנֵנוּ״.
phrases.english: and the one who said 'with shofarot' did not say 'with Aneinu.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the dispute between steps 16 and 17 so it can be challenged.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Working assumption: the two opinions about התרעה exclude each other.

steps.title: The יריחו mnemonic seems to refute the עננו view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says seven fasts include eighteen alarms, with יריחו as the mnemonic. Since יריחו involved שופרות, this seems to refute whoever says the alarm is עננו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: We do not decree fewer than seven fasts on the community, and in them are eighteen alarms. A sign for this is יריחו. And in יריחו there were שופרות, so this is a refutation of the one who said 'with עננו'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge the view of רב. The ברייתא connects the alarms to יריחו, where the walls fell through שופר blasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ties the eighteen alarms of the seven fasts to יריחו. At יריחו the alarm was clearly made with שופרות. So if the fast-day alarm is modeled on יריחו, it should be שופרות, which seems to disprove the view that it is only עננו.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught in a ברייתא?
We do not decree fewer than
A mnemonic (memory sign) for the matter

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge rests on the 'first assumption' of step 18, that the עננו view rejects שופרות entirely. Keep that in mind, because step 20 drops that assumption and answers the challenge.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will reconsider whether the two opinions really exclude each other.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מִשֶּׁבַע תַּעֲנִיּוֹת עַל הַצִּבּוּר,
phrases.english: We do not decree fewer than seven fasts on the community,
which include eighteen alarms.
And a mnemonic for the matter: Jericho.
And in Jericho it was with shofarot,
so this is a refutation of the one who said 'with Aneinu'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מִשֶּׁבַע תַּעֲנִיּוֹת עַל הַצִּבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a ברייתא to attack the עננו opinion, as framed by the assumption in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion of רב (via רב יהודה בריה דרב שמואל בר שילת) that the alarm is עננו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא models the fast-day alarms on יריחו, where the alarm was made with שופרות. So the alarm should be with שופרות, which contradicts the view that it is only עננו.

steps.title: Everyone agrees on שופר; the argument is only about עננו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops its earlier assumption. Both sides agree שופרות are called הַתְרָעָה. They argue only about whether עננו is also called הַתְרָעָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: about שופרות, everyone agrees they are called 'sounding the alarm.' Where they argue is about עננו. One master (רב) holds it is also called 'sounding the alarm,' and the other master (רב יהודה) holds it is not called 'sounding the alarm.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from יריחו by changing how it understands the argument between רב and רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 18 the גמרא assumed each side rejects the other's method. Now it says nobody rejects שופרות, so the proof from יריחו (which used שופרות) no longer hurts רב. The only real argument is whether the prayer עננו also counts as הַתְרָעָה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals that an earlier assumption is being replaced
Everyone agrees (literally: all the world does not disagree)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב now rejects שופרות. After this step, רב agrees שופרות count as הַתְרָעָה. He simply adds עננו as well.

phrases.english: Rather: regarding shofarot,
everyone agrees (does not disagree)
that it is called 'sounding the alarm.'
Where they disagree is about Aneinu.
phrases.notes: עננו is a prayer asking ה׳ to answer us

phrases.english: One master holds: it is called 'sounding the alarm,'

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: לָא קָרֵי לַהּ הַתְרָעָה.
phrases.english: and the other master holds: it is not called 'sounding the alarm.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: בְּשׁוֹפָרוֹת, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19 by rejecting the assumption from Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the scope of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each side rejects the other's method, so the יריחו proof (שופרות) refutes רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone accepts שופרות as הַתְרָעָה. The argument is only whether עננו is also called הַתְרָעָה, so יריחו refutes nobody.

steps.title: Spelling out what each side now holds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states what follows from the new framing. The view that includes עננו certainly includes שופרות. The view that says שופרות excludes עננו.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says the alarm is with עננו, all the more so it is with שופרות. And according to the one who says the alarm is with שופרות, it is with שופרות but not with עננו!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out clearly what each opinion means under the new explanation. This sets up the next challenge against the view that includes עננו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's view now covers both methods, because if even a prayer counts as הַתְרָעָה, a שופר certainly does. רב יהודה's view covers only שופרות. This makes the real difference sharp: does a mouth-prayer count as הַתְרָעָה?

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: According to the one who says it is with Aneinu —
all the more so with shofarot.
And according to the one who says it is with shofarot —
but not with Aneinu!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בַּ״עֲנֵנוּ״ כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן בְּשׁוֹפָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the results of the reframed dispute in Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: both עננו and שופרות are called הַתְרָעָה. רב יהודה: only שופרות are called הַתְרָעָה, not עננו.

steps.title: A ברייתא separates crying out from sounding the alarm
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that for lesser plagues they did not sound the alarm but cried out. Crying out is with the mouth, so sounding the alarm must be with שופרות. This challenges the view that a mouth-prayer like עננו counts as הַתְרָעָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: For all other kinds of calamities that break out, such as scabs, locusts, flies, hornets, mosquitoes, and swarms of snakes and scorpions, they would not sound the alarm, but they would cry out. Since crying out is with the mouth, sounding the alarm must be with שופרות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge the view that עננו is called הַתְרָעָה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא contrasts 'sounding the alarm' with 'crying out.' Crying out is a prayer of the mouth, so הַתְרָעָה must be something else, namely שופרות. That suggests a mouth-prayer like עננו is not הַתְרָעָה, which is the opposite of רב's view.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: But it was taught: and all other kinds of calamities
that break out, such as scabs, locusts,
flies, hornets, and mosquitoes,
and a sending of snakes and scorpions —
they would not sound the alarm, but they would cry out.
Since crying out is with the mouth,
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's inference from the ברייתא

phrases.english: sounding the alarm must be with shofarot!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: וּשְׁאָר כׇּל מִינֵי פּוּרְעָנוּיוֹת הַמִּתְרַגְּשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the view laid out in Step 21 that עננו is called הַתְרָעָה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that the prayer עננו is called הַתְרָעָה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats 'crying out' (a mouth-prayer) as something different from הַתְרָעָה. So הַתְרָעָה means שופרות, and a prayer like עננו is not called הַתְרָעָה.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים, shown from a משנה about שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that whether crying out counts as הַתְרָעָה is an argument between תנאים. A משנה lists emergencies for which one sounds the alarm on שבת, and רבי יוסי limits it to calling for help, not for crying out.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute of תנאים, as we learned in a משנה: For these we sound the alarm on שבת: for a city surrounded by an army or a river, and for a ship tossed about at sea. רבי יוסי says: the alarm is to call for help, but not for crying out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the ברייתא follows one תנא, while רב follows another תנא who disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי separates sounding the alarm 'for help' from 'crying out,' just like the ברייתא does. The first opinion in the משנה does not make that limit, so it can treat crying out as part of הַתְרָעָה, which matches רב. So the ברייתא does not refute רב. It only shows that רב sides with a different תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
As we learned in a משנה
We sound the alarm on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: everyone agrees שופרות are called הַתְרָעָה. Whether the prayer עננו (crying out) is also called הַתְרָעָה is an old dispute. רב יהודה and the ברייתא match רבי יוסי, who separates הַתְרָעָה from crying out. רב matches the other תנא.
steps.whyThisMatters: A strong-looking proof from a ברייתא can be answered by showing that the question was already argued among the תנאים. Then each אמורא simply follows a different תנא.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of tanna'im,
as we learned: for these they sound the alarm on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: עַל עִיר שֶׁהִקִּיפוּהָ גַּיִיס אוֹ נָהָר,
phrases.english: for a city surrounded by an army or a river,
and for a ship tossed about at sea.
Rabbi Yosei says: to summon help,
but not for crying out.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא, דִּתְנַן: עַל אֵלּוּ מַתְרִיעִין בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 22 by tying each view to a different תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves that crying out is never called הַתְרָעָה, which would refute רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows the approach of רבי יוסי, who separates alarm for help from crying out. רב follows the first תנא, who does not make that limit.

steps.title: How was the alarm sounded on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what tool the alarm in the שבת emergency משנה was sounded with.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what do they sound the alarm in that case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the משנה it just quoted: when it says we sound the alarm on שבת, how is that done? This question sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה from Step 23 says one sounds the alarm on שבת for certain emergencies. To use this משנה as a source, the גמרא first has to pin down what 'sounding the alarm' means there. There are only two options: שופרות or the prayer עננו.

keyTerms.meaning: With what? (asking about the means or tool used)

phrases.english: With what?
phrases.notes: A one-word question. It asks how the alarm in the שבת emergency משנה is sounded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts showing that the משנה quoted in Step 23 really contains a תנא who calls עננו a הַתְרָעָה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the הַתְרָעָה in the שבת emergency משנה: שופרות or עננו?

steps.title: It cannot mean שופרות, since שופרות are not blown on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules out שופרות, because blowing שופר is not allowed on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means with שופרות: is blowing שופרות on שבת allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option, that the alarm means blowing שופרות. It rejects it right away, because שופר is not blown on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blowing שופר on שבת is forbidden. Even when ראש השנה falls on שבת, the שופר is not blown. So a משנה that allows sounding the alarm on שבת cannot be talking about שופרות.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (brings up an option, usually to reject it)
Is it permitted? (a rhetorical question meaning 'surely not')

steps.confusionAlert: 'מִי שְׁרֵי' sounds like a real question, but here it means 'of course it is not allowed.' It knocks out the שופרות option.

phrases.english: If you say with shofars —
phrases.notes: The first possible meaning of 'sounding the alarm.'

phrases.english: are shofars permitted on Shabbat?!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question. שופר is not blown on שבת, not even on ראש השנה that falls on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 24 by ruling out the first option.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the הַתְרָעָה of the שבת משנה as שופרות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Blowing שופר on שבת is forbidden, so the משנה could not permit it.

steps.title: So it means the prayer עננו, and it is still called an alarm
steps.stepSummary: Since it cannot be שופרות, it must be the prayer עננו, and the משנה calls that הַתְרָעָה. This proves some תנאים count a mouth-prayer as הַתְרָעָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not that it means with עננו, and the משנה calls it 'sounding the alarm'? Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the alarm on שבת must be the prayer עננו. Since the משנה calls that prayer הַתְרָעָה, this proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With שופרות ruled out, the only option left is עננו. The first opinion in that משנה uses the word הַתְרָעָה for it. This shows there is a תנא who calls a mouth-prayer הַתְרָעָה, so the view of רב יהודה בריה דרב שמואל בר שילת has a תנא to rely on. That answers the challenge from Step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that (introduces the only option left)
The prayer 'Answer us,' said on fast days and in times of trouble
And it calls it (by this name)
Learn from this (a proof is confirmed)

steps.whatToRemember: Whether a prayer like עננו counts as הַתְרָעָה is an argument between תנאים. The first opinion in the שבת emergency משנה calls עננו הַתְרָעָה, because שופר cannot be blown on שבת. רבי יוסי disagrees.
steps.whyThisMatters: It closes the challenge from Step 22. The ברייתא that separates 'crying out' from 'sounding the alarm' follows only one side of an argument between תנאים, so the view that counts עננו as הַתְרָעָה stands.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not with 'Aneinu,'
phrases.notes: The only option left after שופרות was ruled out.

phrases.english: and it calls it 'sounding the alarm,'
phrases.notes: The first opinion in the משנה uses the word הַתְרָעָה for a prayer.

phrases.english: Learn from this.
phrases.notes: This confirms that there is a תנא who calls עננו a הַתְרָעָה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With שופרות ruled out in Step 25, the remaining option, עננו, is shown to be called הַתְרָעָה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is a תנא, the first opinion in the שבת emergency משנה, who calls the prayer עננו a הַתְרָעָה. The view that the alarm can be done with עננו is a valid opinion among תנאים.

steps.title: A time of trouble in the years of רבי יהודה נשיאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new story: during the years of רבי יהודה נשיאה there was a time of trouble.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the years of רבי יהודה נשיאה there was a time of trouble.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about a crisis in the days of רבי יהודה נשיאה. This line only sets the scene; the rest of the story comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof about עננו is finished, so this is a new section. The story fits the topic of fasts and responses to trouble. Here we only learn the time period and that there was a hardship.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה the Prince, the grandson of רבי יהודה הנשיא
Trouble, distress, a hardship facing the community

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי יהודה נשיאה with רבי יהודה הנשיא, who put together the משנה. רבי יהודה נשיאה was his grandson.

phrases.english: In the years of Rabbi Yehuda Nesia
phrases.notes: Gives the time period of the story.

phrases.english: there was a trouble,
phrases.notes: The story continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁנֵי דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה הֲוָה צַעֲרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section after the proof about עננו ended in Step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets the scene: a communal hardship in the days of רבי יהודה נשיאה.
